site.content.principles.browser.body: Parsing, rendering, snapping, hatching and plotting all run on your machine, in the tab. The server holds identity, files and versions. A large drawing does not need a large upload to draw a line.
site.content.principles.browser.title: The browser is enough.
site.content.principles.ownership.body: DXF export is on every plan, including Free. If you stop paying your drawings stay readable and exportable. There is no proprietary format standing between you and your work.
site.content.principles.ownership.title: Your files are yours.
site.content.principles.parity.body: A drawing must open in CADO the way it was issued: same dimension values, same text, same lineweights. When a DXF renders differently from AutoCAD we treat it as a bug and fix the importer, not the drawing.
site.content.principles.parity.title: AutoCAD parity is the bar, not a feature.

site.content.workflow.annotate.body: Dimensions attach to geometry and follow it. Hatch regenerates when its boundary moves. Blocks carry attributes, so a plan can be counted into a schedule with a table instead of retyped.
site.content.workflow.annotate.title: Annotate so it survives edits
site.content.workflow.draft.body: Type L, C, TR or F and answer the same prompts. Fifteen object snaps, ortho and polar tracking and dynamic input next to the cursor keep the geometry exact. Grips, undo and the properties panel behave the way your hands expect.
site.content.workflow.draft.title: Draft with the commands you know
site.content.workflow.layout.body: Add a layout, set the paper, place viewports at 1:50 or 1:100, fill the title block. The same model can carry a general arrangement and a detail sheet without duplicating a line.
site.content.workflow.layout.prompt: _MVIEW Specify corner of viewport: scale 1:50 on A3 landscape
site.content.workflow.layout.title: Lay it out on paper
site.content.workflow.open.body: Drop a file on the dashboard or open it from the editor. Parsing runs in a Web Worker, so a large survey never blocks the UI, and the drawing renders as AutoCAD renders it: dimension values, text, fonts and lineweights included.
site.content.workflow.open.title: Open a DXF, or start blank
site.content.workflow.share.body: Plot to PDF with real lineweights, export SVG or an image, or write the DXF back out with its own layers, blocks and linetypes. Save keeps a version; a share link lets a reviewer open it in their browser too.
site.content.workflow.share.prompt: Saved v14 · exported GA-01.pdf · link copied
site.content.workflow.share.title: Plot, export, share
site.docs.ai.backend.builtin.body: The default. A rule-based parser that understands colours, layers, lineweights, directions and the current selection. Nothing leaves the browser and no setup is needed.
site.docs.ai.backend.builtin.name: Built-in parser
site.docs.ai.backend.ollama.body: Point the panel at a server URL (default http://localhost:11434) and pick a pulled model. Set OLLAMA_ORIGINS so the browser may call it; an https:// deployment cannot reach an http:// server.
site.docs.ai.backend.ollama.name: Ollama
site.docs.ai.backend.openrouter.body: Paste an API key in the panel’s settings. The key is kept in this browser’s localStorage and sent straight to OpenRouter from the browser; a consent notice explains what is shared before the first request.
site.docs.ai.backend.openrouter.name: OpenRouter
site.docs.ai.cap.annotate.dimension: Add a dimension to a selected edge
site.docs.ai.cap.annotate.sheet: Generate a sheet from a library template
site.docs.ai.cap.annotate.symbol: Insert a symbol from the library
site.docs.ai.cap.select.byFilter: Entities by colour, layer, type or the current selection
site.docs.ai.cap.sheets.arrange: Arrange plan, section and detail views
site.docs.ai.cap.sheets.zoom: Zoom to a layer, a selection or extents
site.docs.ai.lede: Type what you want in plain language and the assistant turns it into ordinary editor commands. It proposes, you decide, and everything it does is one Undo away.
site.docs.ai.modelBody: Open the assistant panel and its settings (⚙). Three kinds of backend are offered; the built-in parser needs no setup and is where most people stay.
site.docs.ai.pipeline.classify: Classify. Each tool declares a risk class and the batch takes the highest.
site.docs.ai.pipeline.commit: Commit as one step. The whole batch is a single command on the undo stack. Ctrl+Z removes it entirely.
site.docs.ai.pipeline.confirm: Confirm. Destructive batches wait for a yes; review batches show what they will touch.
site.docs.ai.pipeline.log: Log locally. Every resolved turn goes to an append-only audit log in this browser's IndexedDB. It never leaves your device.
site.docs.ai.pipeline.validate: Validate. The request compiles to named tools; unknown actions, empty targets and missing permissions are rejected before anything runs.
site.docs.ai.privacyNote: Privacy. With the built-in parser or a local Ollama server, nothing about your drawing leaves your machine or network. With OpenRouter, a summary of the drawing (layers, entity counts and types, the current selection, never the raw file) and your prompts are sent to that provider, and only after you have picked the model and acknowledged the notice. site.docs.ai.risk.destructive.body: Deleting or replacing geometry. Always asks for confirmation first.
site.docs.ai.risk.destructive.label: destructive
site.docs.ai.risk.review.body: Reversible edits such as recolouring or relayering. Shown with the affected count before they run.
site.docs.ai.risk.review.label: review
site.docs.ai.risk.safe.body: Reads and navigation: selecting, zooming, describing. Applied at once.
site.docs.ai.risk.safe.label: safe
site.docs.ai.screen.alt: The AI assistant panel docked in the editor, with a conversation, a proposed action and its risk label, and the settings gear.
site.docs.ai.screen.caption: A proposal with its affected count and risk class, before it runs.
site.docs.ai.screen.title: Assistant
site.docs.ai.tryBody: The built-in parser reads a colour as a filter, on layer X as a scope, to layer X as a destination, and “selected”, “these” or “them” as the current selection. When nothing is named and something is selected, the selection is the target.
site.docs.aids.dynamicInput.body: Fields next to the cursor show the length, angle or coordinates the tool is about to use. Type a number and it goes into the field; type a letter to pick a command option without moving to the command line.
site.docs.aids.dynamicInput.name: Dynamic input
site.docs.aids.ortho.body: Constrains the next point to horizontal or vertical from the previous one. Hold Shift to flip it temporarily. Ortho and polar are exclusive; enabling one disables the other.
site.docs.aids.ortho.name: Ortho
site.docs.aids.otrack.body: Acquires points you hover over and projects alignment guides from them, so you can place a point in line with geometry you are not touching.
site.docs.aids.otrack.name: Object snap tracking
site.docs.aids.polar.body: Snaps the cursor to angle increments from the previous point, 15° by default, and labels the locked angle on the guide.
site.docs.aids.polar.name: Polar tracking
site.docs.blocks.define.body: B turns a selection and a base point into a definition; I inserts it with scale and rotation. The Blocks palette lists every definition in the drawing to drag in. Paste as block (Ctrl+Alt+V) defines and places in one step.
site.docs.blocks.define.title: Define and place
site.docs.blocks.edit.body: The block editor opens one definition in isolation; save with BCLOSE or answer the prompt on Esc, and every instance follows. X explodes an instance into plain entities when you need to.
site.docs.blocks.edit.title: Edit the definition
site.docs.blocks.library.body: Blocks carry attributes: imported ATTDEF and ATTRIB values are kept, shown and editable, and FIND searches and replaces across text, MText, attribute values and table cells. The library holds symbols you reuse across drawings.
site.docs.blocks.library.title: Attributes, library, find
site.docs.blocks.title: Blocks, attributes and the library
site.docs.closing.sub: The Free plan has the whole toolset and DXF export. If the editor and this page disagree, tell us which one is wrong.
site.docs.closing.title: Open a DXF and check the manual against it.
site.docs.cloud.conflict.body: Every save carries the version it started from. If the server has a newer one, it refuses rather than overwriting, and you choose:
site.docs.cloud.conflict.copy.body: Keeps both. Your work becomes a new drawing in the same folder and workspace.
site.docs.cloud.conflict.copy.label: Save as copy
site.docs.cloud.conflict.overwrite.body: Saves over the other version. It is still in the version history.
site.docs.cloud.conflict.overwrite.label: Overwrite
site.docs.cloud.conflict.reload.body: Drops your unsaved changes and opens the version the server has.
site.docs.cloud.conflict.reload.label: Reload latest
site.docs.cloud.conflict.title: Someone saved first
site.docs.cloud.foldersBody: My Drawings holds folders you can nest and move; deleting sends a drawing to Trash, where it can be restored or the trash emptied. A view-only drawing still opens in a working editor; when you save, the result goes to a copy of your own.
site.docs.cloud.lede: An account gives you a place for drawings, a version for every save, and a way to hand a drawing to someone else without emailing a file.
site.docs.cloud.offline.body: If the network fails, the save lands in the local cache marked pending and the header says so. Press <kbd class="site-kbd">Ctrl+S</kbd> again when you are back online; replay is deliberately manual so a stale copy is never pushed over someone else's work.
site.docs.cloud.offline.title: Queued in the browser
site.docs.cloud.role.admin.body: Everything a member can, plus invite people and assign viewer, member or admin.
site.docs.cloud.role.admin.name: Admin
site.docs.cloud.role.member.body: Everything a viewer can, plus create, save, rename and trash drawings and folders.
site.docs.cloud.role.member.name: Member
site.docs.cloud.role.owner.body: Everything an admin can, plus transfer ownership. One per organization.
site.docs.cloud.role.owner.name: Owner
site.docs.cloud.role.viewer.body: Opens and downloads the organization’s drawings. Cannot save, rename or trash.
site.docs.cloud.role.viewer.name: Viewer
site.docs.cloud.save.body: Saves are explicit. Each one writes the DXF to your account and mints a new version; the dashboard's version history lists them all and restores any of them. Files up to 50 MB.
site.docs.cloud.save.title: Cloud save, one version
site.docs.cloud.sharingBody: Share a drawing directly with an email address or a whole organization, or make a link. Links are view or edit, expire after 7, 30 or 90 days or never, can be revoked, and can be emailed to up to ten people with a note straight from the dialog. Recipients open the drawing in their browser.
site.docs.cloud.snapshot.body: If anything changed, the drawing is serialised to the browser's IndexedDB. This is crash insurance, not a cloud save: it does not create a version and does not touch the server.
site.docs.cloud.snapshot.title: Recovery snapshot
site.docs.commands.emptyBody: No command matches “{{query}}”. Try the AutoCAD alias, or a word from what the command does.
site.docs.commands.filterPlaceholder: Name, alias or what it does, e.g. fillet, TR, viewport
site.docs.commands.lede: Every command the toolbar shows, with the aliases the command line accepts. Type the alias, press Enter or Space, answer the prompts. {{total}} entries in {{groups}} groups.
site.docs.dxf.lede: Drawings are stored as DXF, so import and export are not converters bolted on the side; they are the file format. The bar is AutoCAD parity: a drawing opens as it was issued, and saves back out with what it came with. Imports run in a Web Worker so a large file never freezes the tab.
site.docs.dxf.limits.dwg.body: A .dwg can be uploaded to the dashboard, versioned and downloaded, but the editor cannot open it yet. Conversion is planned; today you need a DXF to draw.
site.docs.dxf.limits.hatch.body: Where a file stores pattern lines at a different scale from what its own header implies, CADO draws what the file says; AutoCAD Web appears to regenerate the pattern instead, so the two can differ.
site.docs.dxf.limits.mtext.body: One font and one height per entity. A \H or \f code is honoured when it opens the string; a change mid-paragraph is dropped rather than applied to text it never covered.
site.docs.dxf.limits.threeD.body: CADO is a 2D drafter. Z coordinates are read but nothing is modelled or displayed in 3D.
site.docs.dxf.limits.version.body: Export always writes AC1032 (AutoCAD 2018) ASCII DXF. There is no option for an older version or for binary DXF.
site.docs.dxf.parityNote: How parity is checked. AutoCAD bakes each dimension's rendered geometry and final text into an anonymous *D block. CADO's import is compared against those blocks on a real bridge general-arrangement drawing: 384 of 384 dimensions match, and still match after an export and re-import.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.blocks.body: Block definitions, inserts with scale and rotation, ATTDEF and ATTRIB. BYBLOCK colours resolve through the insert. Anonymous *D and *T blocks are kept.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.dimensions.body: DIMSTYLE table, per-entity DIMLFAC and DIMSCALE overrides read from XDATA, DIMDEC, DIMCLRD/E/T, rotated dimensions, the stored text midpoint, \X stacked text. Verified against the *D blocks AutoCAD writes.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.hatch.body: Solid and pattern hatches with their embedded pattern definitions, so a pattern the registry has never heard of still renders from the file. Clockwise and elliptical edges are handled.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.layers.body: Name, colour, on/off, frozen, locked, linetype and lineweight. The drawing’s own LTYPE table and $LTSCALE are read and written, so dashes come back at the same length.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.ocs.body: The extrusion normal (OCS) is honoured, so entities AutoCAD mirrored onto the (0,0,−1) plane land where they belong.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.other.body: Entity types the editor has no model for are kept as raw records and written back unchanged, so a save does not strip what it did not understand.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.polylines.body: Vertices, bulges, constant and tapered widths (which is how AutoCAD draws a filled arrowhead).
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.tables.body: ACAD_TABLE renders from its block. Paper-space VIEWPORTs become the layout’s viewports and write back. OLE2FRAME signature stamps are shown and re-emitted verbatim.
site.docs.dxf.roundtrip.text.body: STYLE table with per-style fonts, %% escapes, MText formatting codes (\P, \pxq, \Q, \W, \U+XXXX), justification anchored at group 11, oblique and width factor. Pre-R2007 files are decoded with their $DWGCODEPAGE.
site.docs.embedding.lede: The editor is a standalone Angular component with a small API. There are three ways to put it in front of your users.
site.docs.embedding.one.body: Deploy CADO on its own origin and link to a stored drawing with /editor/<drawingId>, or to a blank one with /editor. Nothing to integrate; this is what most teams should do first.
site.docs.embedding.one.title: 1. Run it separately and link to it
site.docs.embedding.three.body: DrawingTransferService is an inbox that survives a page refresh. Set the payload, navigate to the editor, and it opens the drawing on start-up. Storage keys are prefixed cad.transfer.*.
site.docs.embedding.three.payloads: Accepted payloads: DXF text (AC1032 headers are validated; older files still parse) and the JSON entity payloads produced by the cad-core exporters.
site.docs.embedding.three.title: 3. Hand a drawing over between pages
site.docs.embedding.two.body: CadEditorComponent takes a drawing id or DXF text and emits the DXF back when the user exports or leaves.
site.docs.embedding.two.mode: Embedded mode. Leave the Supabase URL and anon key empty in the environment file. Route guards pass through, the account menu renders nothing, and a 401 from the API no longer redirects to a sign-in page: your application owns identity. Link users straight at /editor; the dashboard is not meant for this mode. If your app mints its own tokens, override the token source:
site.docs.embedding.two.title: 2. Embed the component
site.docs.embedding.two.token: getToken() may return a string, null, or a promise of either. Your provider owns expiry; in embedded mode the editor will not navigate on a 401.
site.docs.hero.lede: From the first sign-in to embedding the editor in your own product. Each section is written from the code, not from a plan; if something here is wrong, the editor is wrong too.
site.docs.hero.note: Twelve sections on one page. The sidebar follows you, every heading has a link, and the command table filters as you type.
site.docs.hero.title: Everything the editor does, in the order you will need it.
site.docs.languages.changeNoteAfter: . The option names are in each language's own script on purpose.
site.docs.languages.chosen1: The language this browser last chose, if any.
site.docs.languages.chosen2: Otherwise the browser's own language preferences, widened (de-AT becomes Deutsch).
site.docs.languages.chosen4: Signing in applies the language stored on your account on top, so it follows you across devices.
site.docs.languages.lede: The interface, command prompts included, ships in the fourteen languages AutoCAD ships in, so a drafter finds both their language and their terminology. Command aliases stay as they are in every language.
site.docs.languages.statusNote: Translation status. English is the source. The other thirteen files are drafted following AutoCAD's established terminology per language and have not yet been reviewed by native-speaking drafters. Any string still missing from a language falls back to English rather than showing a key name. If a term reads wrong in your language,
site.docs.layers.body: Open the panel with <kbd class="site-kbd">LA</kbd>. Each layer carries a colour, a linetype and a lineweight that entities inherit ByLayer, and four states you toggle per row. Layer 0 and Defpoints are protected and cannot be deleted; everything comes in from DXF and goes back out unchanged.
site.docs.layers.freeze.body: Frozen layers are skipped by the renderer and by extents as well; use it for reference geometry you never want to see.
site.docs.layers.freeze.name: Freeze / Thaw
site.docs.layers.isolateNote: There is no isolate button in the panel; ask the assistant instead: isolate layer WALLS hides every other layer in one undoable step.
site.docs.layers.lock.body: Locked layers stay visible but their entities are protected from editing.
site.docs.layers.lock.name: Lock / Unlock
site.docs.layers.onOff.body: Layers that are off are not drawn, cannot be picked and are left out of zoom-to-extents.
site.docs.layers.onOff.name: On / Off
site.docs.layers.plot.body: A no-plot layer shows on screen and is left out of PDF, SVG and image output. Defpoints is no-plot by default.
site.docs.layers.plot.name: Plot / No plot
site.docs.layers.screen.alt: The Layers panel open on the right of the editor, listing layers with on/off, freeze, lock and plot toggles, colour swatches, linetype and lineweight.
site.docs.layers.screen.caption: On, freeze, lock, plot, colour, linetype, lineweight. Per layer, per drawing.
site.docs.layers.screen.title: Layers
site.docs.layers.title: Layers
site.docs.layouts.lede: Model space is where you draw at full size. A layout is a sheet of paper with viewports that frame the model at a scale; that is what gets plotted.
site.docs.layouts.pageSetup.body: PAGESETUP sets paper, orientation, plot offset, plot style and scale for the layout, and the same fields appear in the Plot dialog for a one-off. Lineweights can scale with the plot scale or stay absolute.
site.docs.layouts.pageSetup.title: Page setup
site.docs.layouts.plotScreen.alt: The Plot dialog: format, paper size, orientation, plot area, scale and plot style fields with a preview of the sheet.
site.docs.layouts.plotScreen.caption: Window, extents, display or layout; PDF, SVG, PNG or JPG.
site.docs.layouts.plotScreen.title: Plot
site.docs.layouts.scalesBody: Fit to page, a preset, or a custom ratio typed in.
site.docs.layouts.screen.alt: A paper-space layout tab in CADO: a white sheet with a viewport showing the bridge drawing at a fixed scale.
site.docs.layouts.screen.caption: A layout tab: the sheet, one viewport, the model at 1:50.
site.docs.layouts.spaces.body: LAYOUT adds, renames and reorders layout tabs. MVIEW draws a viewport on the sheet and asks for its scale; viewports are objects, so you move them, drag a grip to resize them (scale preserved) and Delete them like anything else. Type MSPACE to pan, zoom and edit the model through the first viewport; PSPACE returns to the sheet, where title blocks and notes live. Every tool works in both spaces, and osnap only picks the space you are editing.
site.docs.layouts.spaces.title: Model space and paper space
site.docs.output.dxf: The drawing itself, written back out. See DXF compatibility.
site.docs.output.pdf: Vector, with lineweights, searchable text and embedded fonts. Publish writes every layout to one PDF.
site.docs.output.raster: Raster at 72 to 1200 DPI, or by long edge at 2K, 4K or 8K.
site.docs.output.svg: Vector export of the plotted area.
site.docs.paper.customNote: Any width and height in mm or inches
site.docs.plotStyle.color.body: Entity and layer colours plot as stored.
site.docs.plotStyle.color.name: Color
site.docs.plotStyle.grayscale.body: Colours are mapped to greys by luminance.
site.docs.plotStyle.grayscale.name: Grayscale
site.docs.plotStyle.monochrome.body: Everything plots black, the way a CTB monochrome table does.
site.docs.plotStyle.monochrome.name: Monochrome
site.docs.shortcuts.aids.dynamicInput: Dynamic input next to the cursor.
site.docs.shortcuts.aids.label: Drafting aids
site.docs.shortcuts.aids.note: The same function keys as AutoCAD. Each one also has a button in the status bar.
site.docs.shortcuts.aids.ortho: Ortho. Turning it on turns polar off.
site.docs.shortcuts.aids.polar: Polar tracking. Turning it on turns ortho off.
site.docs.shortcuts.cmdline.label: Command line
site.docs.shortcuts.cmdline.letters: Type a command alias. While a command runs, a letter picks the option with that key, as in [Close/Undo].
site.docs.shortcuts.cmdline.note: Start typing anywhere and the text lands in the command line; you never have to click it first.
site.docs.shortcuts.cmdline.space: Same as Enter, as in AutoCAD.
site.docs.shortcuts.editing.cancel: Cancel the running command and return to Select. In the block editor, asks whether to save the block.
site.docs.shortcuts.editing.erase: Erase the selection. Inside Polyline or Leader, Backspace removes the last vertex instead.
site.docs.shortcuts.editing.label: Editing
site.docs.shortcuts.editing.note: Undo, redo, select all and the clipboard work wherever focus is, except inside the in-canvas text or table editor, which keep their own history.
site.docs.shortcuts.editing.repeat: With nothing running: repeat the last drawing or modify command.
site.docs.shortcuts.editing.shift: Held: temporary ortho override. In Trim and Extend it swaps to the other tool instead.
site.docs.shortcuts.editing.undo: Undo. One step per command, including anything the assistant did.
site.docs.shortcuts.files.close: Close the active drawing; asks to save first.
site.docs.shortcuts.files.export: Export dialog (the same dialog as Plot, ready for a file).
site.docs.shortcuts.files.label: Files and output
site.docs.shortcuts.files.open: Open: My Drawings, a folder or a local DXF.
site.docs.shortcuts.files.quickPlot: Quick plot with the last settings; opens the dialog if there are none yet.
site.docs.shortcuts.files.save: Save. On a never-saved drawing this becomes Save As.
site.docs.shortcuts.files.saveAs: Save As: a new name, folder or workspace.
site.docs.shortcuts.lede: The bindings below are the ones the editor actually handles. <kbd class="site-kbd">Ctrl</kbd> is <kbd class="site-kbd">⌘</kbd> on a Mac.
site.docs.snapping.lede: Geometry is exact or it is wrong. Fifteen object snaps, two tracking modes and dynamic input keep every point on something.
site.docs.snapping.snapsBody: Toggle them all with <kbd class="site-kbd">F3</kbd>, or turn individual modes on and off from the status bar; the set you choose is remembered. A marker names the snap under the cursor before you click.
site.docs.start.account.body: Sign up with an email address. The Free plan includes the whole toolset and DXF export; you only need a paid plan for more cloud drawings and for organizations.
site.docs.start.account.title: Create an account
site.docs.start.draw.body: Type an alias at the command line and answer the prompts: absolute coordinates as 100,50, relative as @100,50, polar as @3400<90. Every point can snap to geometry, and Enter or Space repeats the last command.
site.docs.start.draw.title: Draw with the commands you know
site.docs.start.embeddedNote: Embedded mode is a deployment option, not a setting. A host application that runs CADO with authentication disabled gets an editor with no sign-in; end users never toggle it. See
site.docs.start.lede: Five steps from nothing to a plotted sheet. Nothing to install; the editor is a page.
site.docs.start.open.body: Drag a .dxf onto the dashboard to upload it into your account, or press Ctrl+O in the editor to open one from My Drawings or your disk. Parsing runs in a Web Worker, so a large survey does not freeze the tab. A blank drawing is one click from Recent.
site.docs.start.open.title: Open a DXF, or start blank
site.docs.start.plot.body: Ctrl+P opens Plot for PDF, SVG, PNG or JPG of a window, the extents, the display or a layout. DXFOUT writes the drawing back out as DXF with its own layers, blocks, linetypes and dimension styles.
site.docs.start.plot.title: Plot or export
site.docs.start.save.body: Ctrl+S saves to your account and keeps a version you can restore from the dashboard. Independently of that, a recovery snapshot is written to the browser every 30 seconds in case the tab dies.
site.docs.start.save.title: Save a version
site.docs.start.screen.alt: The CADO editor with a bridge general-arrangement DXF open on the Model tab: toolbar at the top, command line and status bar at the bottom, layers and properties panels on the right.
site.docs.start.screen.caption: Toolbar, canvas, command line, status bar. The layout AutoCAD users expect.

site.features.caps.blocks.alt: One door block definition placed three times along a wall
site.features.caps.blocks.body: Draw a door once, then place it forty times. Every instance points back at one definition, so correcting the original corrects the drawing — and attributes let each instance carry its own tag, which is what turns a plan into a schedule.
site.features.caps.blocks.title: Blocks and attributes
site.features.caps.dimensions.alt: A rectangle being stretched, with its dimension updating from 2200 millimetres
site.features.caps.dimensions.body: A dimension is attached to the geometry, not typed next to it. Stretch the wall and the measurement updates itself — which is the difference between a drawing you can trust and a drawing you have to re-check. Fifteen object snaps, dimension styles, hatch and tables come with it.
site.features.caps.dimensions.title: Associative dimensions
site.features.caps.dxf.alt: A DXF file opening in the editor and exporting back out to DXF
site.features.caps.dxf.body: Open a file from your desk, edit it, write it back out. Layers, blocks, dimension styles and text all survive the trip, so {{appName}} slots into a toolchain that already runs on DXF instead of asking everyone to move.
site.features.caps.dxf.title: DXF round-trip
site.features.caps.layouts.alt: A paper-space sheet with two viewports and a titleblock
site.features.caps.layouts.body: Model space is where you draw; paper space is where you decide what gets printed. Place viewports at a real scale, fill in the titleblock, and plot the sheet to PDF or SVG — the same drawing can carry a detail sheet and a general arrangement without duplicating any geometry.
site.features.caps.layouts.title: Layouts and viewports
site.features.caps.lede: Scroll and each one draws itself, in the order you would draft it.
site.features.caps.title: Four things a drafting tool has to get right.
site.features.closing.sub: The editor is free to use and DXF export is not behind a paywall. Sign up, drop a file, start typing commands.
site.features.closing.title: Open a drawing and try every one of these.
site.features.commands.lede: Type the alias at the command line or click the tool; the prompts that follow are the ones AutoCAD users expect, in fourteen languages.
site.features.commands.title: Every group, every command, its alias.
site.features.compare.caption: CADO compared with installed desktop CAD
site.features.compare.lede: Where CADO is ahead, where it is level, and where it is honestly not there yet.
site.features.compare.title: A browser tab against an installed seat.
site.features.details.dimstyles.body: A dimension is attached to the geometry it measures; stretch the wall and the value updates. DXF dimension styles import with their arrowheads, text height and precision, and per-dimension overrides in XDATA (including the plot-scale factor DIMLFAC) are honoured, so an imported drawing shows the values AutoCAD shows.
site.features.details.dimstyles.title: Are dimensions really associative, and do dimension styles survive import?
site.features.details.languages.body: Fourteen: the same set AutoCAD ships, command prompts included. English, Čeština, Deutsch, Español, Français, Magyar, Italiano, 日本語, 한국어, Polski, Português (Brasil), Русский, 简体中文 and 繁體中文. Translations other than English are drafted from established AutoCAD terminology and not yet professionally reviewed.
site.features.details.languages.title: Which languages does the interface speak?
site.features.details.layouts.body: Yes. Each layout tab has its own page setup (paper, orientation, margins, scale, plot style) and any number of viewports at their own scales. Viewports defined in an imported DXF are adopted and written back on export.
site.features.details.layouts.title: Can I have more than one layout, each with its own paper?
site.features.details.lineweights.body: Yes. Entities carry ACI colours and true lineweights, lineweights are honoured on screen and in the PDF, and a drawing whose default colour is white on a dark theme plots black on the white sheet, the same swap AutoCAD makes. site.useCases.detail.architects.week1: Drop the consultant’s DXF on the dashboard. It parses in a background worker and opens with its layers, blocks, linetypes and dimension styles intact.
site.useCases.detail.architects.week2: Draw the new work on your own layers: LA to create them, PL and O for walls at an offset, TR and F to clean the junctions, H to hatch the new build.
site.useCases.detail.architects.week3: Make a door once with B, give it attributes, place it with I. Change the definition in BEDIT and every instance follows.
site.useCases.detail.architects.week4: Add a layout, choose A1, place viewports with MV at 1:100 for the plan and 1:20 for the detail, then set the sheet up with PAGESETUP.
site.useCases.detail.architects.week5: PLOT the sheet to PDF with lineweights, DXFOUT the model back to the consultant, and send the client a view-only link.

site.useCases.detail.builders.week1: Deploy CADO on its own origin and link to /editor, or mount <app-cad-editor> inside your Angular application.
site.useCases.detail.builders.week2: Leave the Supabase keys empty. The editor runs in embedded mode: no sign-in, guards pass through, a 401 never redirects to our pages.
site.useCases.detail.builders.week3: Provide AUTH_TOKEN_PROVIDER from your own session service so the API calls carry your token, minted on demand if you like.
site.useCases.detail.builders.week4: Hand a drawing over with initialDxf, or through DrawingTransferService when it comes from another page of yours.
site.useCases.detail.builders.week5: Receive the DXF back on (save) and store it wherever you keep files. Nothing about the format is ours.

site.useCases.detail.engineers.week1: Open the bridge GA. Dimension values, plot-scale overrides, per-style fonts and layer lineweights import as AutoCAD wrote them, so the sheet reads as issued.
site.useCases.detail.engineers.week2: Check a span with DI, then open the properties panel with PR to read the layer, linetype and dimension style of anything you select.
site.useCases.detail.engineers.week3: Isolate the reinforcement layer from the Layers panel, freeze what is in the way, and mark the changed member with a DIMLINEAR and an MLD note.
site.useCases.detail.engineers.week4: Set the precision and units of the dimension style once with DIMSTYLE rather than editing each value.
site.useCases.detail.engineers.week5: PLOT to PDF with lineweights honoured, or PUBLISH every layout to one file. Each Ctrl+S keeps a version you can restore from the dashboard.

site.useCases.detail.students.week1: Create a free account and open the editor on whatever the room has: a Chromebook, a shared lab machine, a laptop at home. There is nothing to install.
site.useCases.detail.students.week2: Follow the tutor’s commands as typed: L, C, TR, F answer the same prompts as AutoCAD. F3 toggles object snaps, F8 ortho, F12 dynamic input.
site.useCases.detail.students.week3: Dimension the exercise with DIM and set the style with DIMSTYLE. Move a wall and watch the dimension follow it.
site.useCases.detail.students.week4: Draw a door once, make it a block with B, place it forty times with I. Fix the definition in BEDIT and every one updates.
site.useCases.detail.students.week5: Hand in a PDF plotted at a real scale and the DXF itself, which opens in the department’s AutoCAD with the same layers.

site.useCases.detail.teams.week2: Two people press Ctrl+S on the same drawing. The second gets Overwrite, Save as copy or Reload instead of a silent overwrite.
site.useCases.detail.teams.week3: Something went wrong on Wednesday. Open version history on the dashboard, pick Tuesday’s save, restore it.
site.useCases.detail.teams.week4: Ask the assistant to “isolate WALLS” or “change every red line on DIM to blue”. It shows the action, labels it safe, review or destructive, and every result is undoable.

site.useCases.explorer.heading: Who uses CADO
site.useCases.hero.lede: Plans, general arrangements, coursework, a studio’s shared set, a drafting surface inside someone else’s product. Five ways CADO is used, with the commands, the files and the plan that fit each.
site.useCases.hero.title: Built for the people who still draw in 2D.
site.useCases.plan.free.why: The full drafting toolset, DXF in and out, PDF and PNG plotting. Enough for coursework and the drawing you open twice a year.
site.useCases.plan.pro.who: Architects and engineers who draw most weeks
site.useCases.plan.pro.why: Unlimited cloud drawings, ninety days of version history, layouts, blocks and dimension styles, and the AI assistant.
site.useCases.plan.team.who: Studios working on the same set of drawings
site.useCases.plan.team.why: Shared folders, view and edit links, unlimited version history and one bill for everyone.

site.useCases.switch.lede: Most of what your hands know still works. The rest is different because a browser and a cloud account are different from an installer and a network share, and we would rather say so than let you find out.
site.useCases.switch.title: What carries over, and what does not.
